title: Incidents: Severity to Learning
objective: After this lesson you will be able to classify incident severity, execute runbooks (contain → assess → roll back), communicate during incidents, and run blameless postmortems that produce gold items, gates, and owners.
why: Every production agent fails eventually: wrong refunds, data leaks, cost explosions, silent quality collapse. Response quality decides whether incidents cost hours or quarters — severity routing, practiced runbooks, safe rollbacks, and learning that ships prevention. On-call for AI systems differs from classic ops in exactly one way: failures are often behavioral (fluent wrongness), so detection starts with the Ch.7 signals, not status codes.

blocks.text: Classify by harm, not noise: **SEV-1** (money moving wrongly, data leaking, active abuse — all hands, contain in minutes), **SEV-2** (quality collapse, cost explosion, single-feature outage — urgent, hours), **SEV-3** (latency drift, minor misroutes — next sprint). Severity routes paging, staffing, and review depth. Mis-severed incidents (SEV-3 paged as SEV-1) burn on-call trust; under-severed ones (leak as SEV-3) burn users.

blocks.caption: Severity by harm class with paging + SLA attached

blocks.text: Runbooks sequence the worst day: **contain** (feature-flag the path off — seconds, reversible), **assess** (blast radius from audit logs: who/what amounts), **roll back** (previous gold-passing version redeployed; scope revoked if abuse). Practice quarterly via game-days (simulated wrong-refund, timed). Runbooks unpracticed are documentation; practiced, they're reflexes.

blocks.caption: Evidence-gated steps: contain → assess → roll back → verify

blocks.text: Postmortems produce **artifacts, not blame**: timeline, root cause (system, never person), the gold item fossilizing the failure, the gate/guardrail preventing recurrence, and an owner with a date. 'Human error' conclusions are banned — humans err; systems allow errors to reach users. The postmortem that ships nothing teaches nothing; the one shipping gold + gates compounds.

blocks.title: Sever the incident
blocks.note: Run it: expect 5/5 — money/data/abuse page as SEV-1, quality/cost as SEV-2, drift rides SEV-3 silently. Severity routes paging, staffing, and review depth.

items: Severity by harm (money/data/abuse → SEV-1 paging; quality/cost → SEV-2; drift → SEV-3)
Runbooks: contain → assess → roll back → verify, evidence-gated, game-day practiced
Blameless postmortems shipping gold + gates + owners; 'human error' banned as a conclusion

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice severifier on all five cases and map levels. (b) Write the contain step for a wrong-refund incident (exact flag/action, seconds-scale). (c) Draft the postmortem artifact list for it (timeline, root cause shape, gold item, gate, owner+date) — with 'human error' explicitly excluded as a conclusion.
hints: Mappings: 1/1/2/2/3 with paging on 1-2 only. Latency drift rides silently to sprint.
Contain: flag refunds-v2 off (kill switch, seconds, reversible) — before any investigation.
Artifacts: timeline from audit logs; root cause systemic (missing amount gate); gold attack item; gate added; owner + date.
exercise.why: Severity mapping (harm→level→paging), containment reflex (flag before forensics), and prevention artifacts (gold+gates+owners) are the three incident judgments — each concrete, never heroic.
exercise.code: // Incident pattern: sever → contain → assess → roll back → fossilize.

quiz.q: Wrong refunds issuing now. First action?
options: Contain: kill-switch the refund path off in seconds — investigation follows containment, never precedes
quiz.explain: Bleeding stops before diagnosis: reversible containment first, forensics second. Investigation during active harm extends it.

options: Banned conclusion: humans err, systems allow errors through — rewrite as missing gate/check/automation with owner + date
quiz.explain: Blameless means systemic: every human error implies an absent guardrail, check, or automation. Conclusions ship prevention artifacts.

quiz.q: Latency drift for a month, no page. Correct?
options: Correct SEV-3 handling: drift rides to sprint planning — paging it would burn on-call trust for non-urgent decay
quiz.explain: Severity routes urgency: drift is SEV-3 by design (sprint, not pager). Over-paging trains teams to ignore pages.

summary: Sever by harm, contain in seconds, assess from logs, roll back safely, fossilize into gold + gates + owners. Incidents handled by reflex, learned from by structure.
